implemented_requirements.requirement: Two-player vertical paddles with independent controls
implemented_requirements.evidence: paddle.py defines Paddle class with up_key/down_key; Game.__init__ creates left paddle (W/S) and right paddle (UP/DOWN) and stores them in self.paddles.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball moves, bounces off top/bottom edges
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.update checks self.y <= 0 and self.y >= WINDOW_HEIGHT - self.size and reverses self.vy accordingly.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball collides with paddles and changes direction with angle based on hit offset
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.update iterates over paddles and calls _bounce_off_paddle; _bounce_off_paddle uses _hit_offset and _set_velocity to reflect horizontally and steer vertically.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Scoring when a player misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.out_of_bounds returns -1 or +1 when the ball leaves the screen; Game.update checks this and calls _after_point, which updates Scoreboard via score_left/score_right.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Winning score threshold and game‑over state
implemented_requirements.evidence: constants.WINNING_SCORE = 5; Scoreboard.has_winner checks against it; Game._after_point switches to STATE_GAME_OVER when has_winner() is true and displays a winner banner.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball reset after each point and serve direction
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game._after_point calls self.ball.reset(self.serve_direction) after awarding a point and before entering STATE_SERVING.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Main entry point to run the game
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py defines main() that creates Game() and calls run(); guarded by if __name__ == "__main__".

critical_issues: No major functional defects detected. The only minor omission is that paddles are not automatically re‑centered after each point (only on full match restart), but this does not affect core gameplay.
judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete two‑player Pong game with controllable paddles, ball physics, scoring, a winning score limit, and ball reset after points. All core requirements are satisfied and the code appears syntactically correct and ready to run with pygame, leading to a pass verdict.
